# OpenCV AI Competition 2026, powered by AWS

## Join, build, and win

Turn an ambitious idea into a working vision application, demonstrate measurable value, and share it with the global OpenCV community.

The competition emphasizes Physical AI and Generative AI systems in which visual understanding drives useful decisions, actions, predictions, or interactions. Any programming language or supporting hardware is allowed.

Projects may use any programming language or supporting hardware, provided they meet the core OpenCV 5 and AWS requirements.

## Focus Paths

Pursue either path, combine both, or take another approach — all entries remain fully eligible for the Overall Awards.

### Cloud-Optimized Vision with COOL

Use the Cloud-Optimized OpenCV Library (COOL) , available through AWS Marketplace and optimized for AWS Graviton, to accelerate widely used vision operations and move from prototype to scalable cloud deployment. Strong submissions will document a reproducible deployment and comparison against an appropriate baseline. Strong submissions will:

- Show that COOL executes the core image or video workload on the Arm path.

- Report reproducible measurements such as latency, throughput, utilization, cost, or developer productivity against an appropriate baseline.

- Explain any x86 and Arm coexistence, container, server, or serverless architecture.

- COOL must execute the claimed core workload on AWS Graviton or the Arm component of a documented hybrid architecture.

### Agentic Vision with OpenCV 5

Build a workflow in which an agent uses OpenCV 5 tools within a multi-step perception-decision-action loop. To qualify, image or video results must influence a subsequent plan, tool call, action, or request for human approval. A chatbot that only explains a fixed vision result is not enough—the visual evidence must change what the system does next.

- Examples include autonomous inspection, visual troubleshooting, embodied assistants, active perception, safety monitoring, and human-in-the-loop operations.

- The agent may use any framework or model and may invoke OpenCV 5 and, where applicable, COOL through APIs, tools, or Model Context Protocol (MCP).

- A developer-agent workflow qualifies only when it iteratively invokes, evaluates, and adjusts an OpenCV 5 workload, with COOL where applicable—for example, by using visual test outputs or runtime measurements to change a later tool call, configuration, or deployment—and culminates in a running image or video workload.

- Using an AI coding assistant to write the entry does not itself qualify as Agentic Vision.

## How The Competition Works

Begins Aug 12. Form a team of up to four members and submit a written proposal to get an AWS Compute Grant.

Aug 18 Onward. Up to 50 teams selected for a grant; notices to be sent to awarded teams.

Aug 26 – Oct 26. Midpoint check-ins Sep 21 – Oct 2 for grant recipients.

Oct 27 – Nov 9 judges will review submissions and rank them. Winners announced Nov 10.

## What AWS Grant Proposals Must Include

Each proposal must include:

- A team name

- A clear problem statement and intended real-world impact.

- The planned OpenCV 5 image or video analysis.

- The planned AWS architecture and services.

- A high-level architecture diagram or technical description.

- The target users or beneficiaries.

- The proposed evaluation method and judge demonstration.

- Whether the team intends to pursue the COOL path, the Agentic Vision path, both, or neither.

- Team Bio: A short team bio of all team members and their participation in any hackathons or competitions. Team strength will be used to judge the recipients of the cloud compute grant.

The organizers will review proposals from August 18 and select up to 50 teams to receive the cloud compute grant based on the strength of the proposed idea and the team’s ability to execute it. Recipient notices will be sent by email to the team leader. Teams that are not selected for a cloud compute grant are encouraged to continue in the competition and are still eligible for prizes.

## Cloud Compute Grant Recipient Selection Criteria

- OpenCV 5 and core image/video fit — weighted 20%

- Technical and AWS feasibility — weighted 20%

- Innovation — weighted 20%

- Real-world impact — weighted 20%

- Team strength, complementary skills, and relevant previous work — weighted 10%

- Evaluation and demonstration plan — weighted 10%

- Ties will be resolved first by the higher OpenCV 5 fit score, then technical and AWS feasibility, then team strength and relevant previous work.

## Free AWS Credits for New Accounts

New AWS customers are eligible to receive $100 in AWS Free Tier credits when they sign up for a Free Plan account and may earn up to $100 more through eligible activities. Teams may use these credits for eligible AWS services in this competition, subject to current AWS Free Tier terms , service availability, and expiration rules. Use of the Free Tier Credits is subject to the AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions . AWS Promotional Credits are not redeemable for cash and can only be applied to AWS Services.

## Build Phase Details

From August 26 through October 26, all teams that submitted the required proposal will build, evaluate, document, and submit their final projects.

- Teams are encouraged to join the official Slack channel to collaborate with others, and to use the #OpenCVComp26 hashtag on social media to share progress and milestones.

- Teams who received a cloud compute grant must complete one 30-minute Zoom check-in with an organizing committee member during September 21–October 2 to receive the other 50% of their grant.

- Teams must maintain active development and provide a concise progress update at the check-in.

- Final submissions are due on October 26 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.

## Final Judging Guidelines

Judges will be selected from the AI and computer vision community. AWS may nominate up to two judges. Eligible final entries will be scored on the following 100-point rubric.

Each final entry will receive at least two independent, conflict-free scores. Final rankings will use the average of those scores. Judges must disclose conflicts and recuse themselves. Entries opting into a Special Award will be scored separately under that award’s rubric.

### Overall Rubric

- Technical execution — weighted 30%: correctness and depth of the OpenCV 5 implementation, architecture, reliability, and evaluation.

- Innovation — weighted 20%: originality and thoughtful use of computer vision or AI.

- Real-world impact — weighted 20%: importance of the problem, usefulness, and evidence of potential benefit.

- User experience — weighted 10%: usability, accessibility, and quality of interaction.

- Documentation and presentation — weighted 10%: clarity of the report, code, architecture, instructions, and video.

- Cloud delivery, reproducibility, and responsible operation — weighted 10%: AWS deployment quality, repeatability, observability, security, and responsible-use practices.

- COOL or agentic methods are not required for the Overall Awards. When present, judges will credit them within the applicable overall criteria only to the extent that they improve the project.

### Best Use of COOL Award Rubric

- Verified COOL integration on AWS Graviton, or on the Arm component of a documented hybrid architecture — weighted 30%.

- Architecture and technical quality — weighted 25%.

- Measured performance, cost, reliability, or developer-productivity value — weighted 20%.

- Innovation — weighted 15%.

- Reproducibility and demonstration — weighted 10%.

### Agentic Vision Award Rubric

- Substantive OpenCV 5 and agent integration — weighted 30%.

- Orchestration and appropriate autonomy — weighted 25%.

- Task effectiveness and evaluation — weighted 20%.

- Failure handling, observability, security, and human control — weighted 15%.

- User experience, documentation, and demonstration — weighted 10%.

Judges’ decisions are final. Overall-ranking ties will be resolved first by Technical Execution, then Real-World Impact, then a conflict-free additional judge scoring all tied entries under the same rubric. Special-award ties will be resolved by the first criterion in the applicable rubric, then the second, then a conflict-free additional judge.
